newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran sees non-oil exports up 9 pct to $3.5 bln.
newsitem.headline: Iran sees non-oil exports up 9 pct to $3.5 bln.

text.p: Iran expects its exports of non-oil goods to reach $3.5 billion in the current Iranian year, up about 9 percent on last year, a senior official said on Friday.
Deputy Trade Minister Ali Saeedlou told the Iranian news agency IRNA that the exports were expected to reach $3.5 billion in the year to March 20, 1997.
The figure would be 9.4 percent higher than the previous year when non-oil exports stood at about $3.2 billion.

Saeedlou said Iran expected to earn another $1.5 billion in the year by providing technical and engineering services to other countries, the agency added. He did not give comparative figures for previous years.
Non-oil exports, dominated by traditional products such as Persian carpets and pistachios, plunged last year by about a quarter from some $4.5 billion in the previous year.

The fall has been blamed on tough foreign exchange controls imposed in May 1995 under which Iran banned free currency exchange, setting a fixed rate of 3,000 rials to the dollar, and told exporters to exchange their hard cash income at the official rate in state banks.
The move was aimed at boosting the value of the Iranian currency which had fallen to as low as 7,000 to the dollar after the United States announced a trade and investment ban on Iran.
Iran, the world's third largest oil exporter, said last month it expected revenue from oil exports this year to reach $18 billion, exceeding budget forecasts by $2 billion.
